name: ballerina/pdf
description: The `ballerina/pdf` module provides functionality to convert HTML content to PDF documents and read data from existing PDFs. It processes HTML strings — including full documents, fragments, and messy real-world markup — and produces PDF byte arrays suitable for writing to files or sending over the network.
readme:
The `ballerina/pdf` module provides functionality to convert HTML content to PDF documents and read data from existing PDFs. It processes HTML strings — including full documents, fragments, and messy real-world markup — and produces PDF byte arrays suitable for writing to files or sending over the network. All processing is done locally with no external service dependencies. ## Quickstart To use the `pdf` connector in your Ballerina application, modify the `.bal` file as follows: ### Step 1: Import the module Import the `pdf` module. ```ballerina import ballerina/pdf; ``` ### Step 2: Invoke module functions #### Extract text from a PDF ```ballerina byte[] pdfBytes = check io:fileReadBytes("document.pdf"); string[] pages = check pdf:extractText(pdfBytes); foreach int i in 0 ..< pages.length() { io:println("Page ", i + 1, ": ", pages[i]); } ``` #### Convert PDF pages to images ```ballerina byte[] pdfBytes = check io:fileReadBytes("document.pdf"); string[] base64Images = check pdf:toImages(pdfBytes); // Each element is a Base64-encoded PNG string (one per page) ``` #### Convert html to pdf Convert an HTML string to a PDF document. ```ballerina byte[] pdfBytes = check pdf:parseHtml("

Hello World

Generated with Ballerina.

"); check io:fileWriteBytes("output.pdf", pdfBytes); ``` #### Convert with custom options ```ballerina string html = check io:fileReadString("report.html"); byte[] pdfBytes = check pdf:parseHtml(html, fallbackFontSize = 10.0, pageSize = pdf:LETTER, margins = {top: 72, right: 54, bottom: 72, left: 54}, additionalCss = "body { font-family: sans-serif; } .container { width: 100% !important; }" ); check io:fileWriteBytes("report.pdf", pdfBytes); ``` ### Step 3: Run the Ballerina application ```bash bal run ``` ## Examples The `pdf` module provides practical examples illustrating usage in various scenarios. Explore these [examples](https://github.com/ballerina-platform/module-ballerina-pdf/tree/main/examples/). 1. [HTML to PDF conversion](https://github.com/ballerina-platform/module-ballerina-pdf/tree/main/examples/html-to-pdf/) — Reads an HTML report file and converts it to PDF. ## Known limitations (HTML-to-PDF conversion) The `parseHtml` function uses a custom HTML/CSS renderer that supports CSS 2.1 core layout (block, inline, float, table, absolute/relative positioning) but has gaps compared to browser rendering. Key limitations: - **Layout:** No flexbox, CSS Grid, or multi-column layout. No `position: fixed` or `position: sticky`. - **Tables:** No `rowspan`, no ``, no `table-layout: fixed` algorithm. - **Text:** No `text-align: justify`, no hyphenation, no `text-indent`, no `text-overflow: ellipsis`. - **CSS features:** No `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements, no CSS counters, no `calc()`, no custom properties (`var()`), no `@import`, no `@media` queries (print/all media types are supported). - **Visual:** No CSS gradients, no `text-shadow`, no CSS transforms, no SVG rendering. Only `solid` border style is supported. - **Fonts:** No `@font-face` (use the `customFonts` option instead). No OpenType features. Bundled fonts: Liberation Sans and Liberation Serif (metrically compatible with Arial and Times New Roman). - **Page control:** No `page-break-inside: avoid`, no orphans/widows control, no `@page` margin boxes.

typeDefs.name: Error
typeDefs.description: Base error type for all PDF module errors.

typeDefs.name: HtmlParseError
typeDefs.description:
Error during HTML parsing or preprocessing.
Returned when the input HTML cannot be parsed into a valid DOM.

typeDefs.name: RenderError
typeDefs.description: Error during the PDF rendering pipeline (layout, painting, or PDF generation).

typeDefs.name: ReadError
typeDefs.description:
Error during PDF reading operations (text extraction, image conversion).
Returned when the input PDF is corrupted, inaccessible, or invalid.

typeDefs.name: StandardPageSize
typeDefs.description: Standard page size presets for PDF output.

typeDefs.name: CustomPageSize
typeDefs.description: Custom page dimensions in points (1 point = 1/72 inch).

typeDefs.name: PageSize
typeDefs.description: Page size for PDF output. Use a standard preset or specify custom dimensions in points.

typeDefs.name: PageMargins
typeDefs.description:
Page margins in points (1 point = 1/72 inch). 
This is the default margin for the PDF output.

typeDefs.name: Font
typeDefs.description: A custom font to register for PDF conversion.

fields.name: family
fields.description: CSS font-family name used to reference this font in HTML/CSS

fields.name: content
fields.description: TTF font file content as bytes

fields.name: bold
fields.description: Whether this is a bold variant (default: false)

fields.name: italic
fields.description: Whether this is an italic variant (default: false)

fields.name: fallbackFontSize
fields.description:
Fallback font size in points (default: 12.0, per CSS spec "medium" keyword).
Used when CSS does not specify a font-size for an element. CSS `font-size`
declarations in the HTML take precedence over this value.

fields.name: pageSize
fields.description:
Page size for the PDF output. Use a standard preset (A4, LETTER, LEGAL)
or a CustomPageSize record with custom width/height in points. When omitted,
the CSS `@page` size rule is used if present, otherwise defaults to A4.

fields.name: margins
fields.description:
Page margins in points (top, right, bottom, left). When omitted, the CSS
`@page` margin rule is used if present, otherwise defaults to 0 (no page margin).

fields.name: additionalCss
fields.description:
Additional CSS to inject into the document before conversion.
Use this for consumer-specific style overrides without modifying the HTML.

fields.name: customFonts
fields.description:
Custom fonts to register for the conversion. Each entry specifies the font family,
TTF content, and weight/style flags. CSS references the font via `font-family`.

fields.name: maxPages
fields.description:
Maximum number of pages in the output PDF. Content is scaled to fit within
this page limit. Must be greater than 0 when provided.

functions.description: Extracts text content from each page of a PDF document.

parameters.name: pdf
parameters.description: The PDF document as a byte array

return.description: An array of text strings (one per page), or an error
